newsitem.title: USA: Rev. Benjamin Chavis joins Farrakhan group.
newsitem.headline: Rev. Benjamin Chavis joins Farrakhan group.

text.p: The Rev. Benjamin Chavis, the ousted former leader of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People, has joined Louis Farrakhan's Nation of Islam but is not the probable successor of the fiery minister, the group said on Monday.
"We expect (Chavis) to be a minister in the Nation of Islam," said Richard Muhammad, editor of the Farrakhan group's newspaper, "The Final Call."
"He is not denouncing Christ or the foundation of his ministry," Muhammad added when asked about Chavis' current role as an ordained minister in the United Church of Christ.
Chavis, in a speech to the group's annual Saviour's Day meeting in Chicago on Sunday, said, "I am not turning from Christ. I am turning to Allah."
Muhammad dismissed as speculation a published report in the Wall Street Journal that said Chavis, 49, was now well-placed to succeed the 69-year-old Farrakhan.

"I don't know where this speculation about a successor comes from. We're happy to have (Chavis) as a member of the Nation of Islam. He has helped Minister Farrakhan and he's always been on the point" of African-American civil rights, Muhammad said in a telephone interview.
Muhammad said Farrakhan was healthy and fully recovered from prostate cancer, which afflicted him several years ago.

Chavis has had close ties to Farrakhan and the relationship has grown stronger since Chavis left the NAACP in 1994 under a cloud after secretly using the group's funds to settle sexual harassment and discrimination accusations.
Chavis was among several speakers on Saviour's Day that included Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi and Nigerian leader Sani Abacha, who spoke to the audience of 6,000 by satellite.

Farrakhan, who has recently visited both African countries in spite of U.S. government travel bans, said that since the end of the Cold War, the American government has taken its "symbols of evil ... from the Islamic world."
